chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I asked him about the man who has intercourse with the slave girl during the month of Ramadan, then he sleeps before he performs the ritual bath. He said: 'He completes his fast and makes up for that day, unless he wakes up before the dawn rises. So if he waits for the water to be warmed or drawn, and the dawn rises, then he does not make up for his day.'

key_terms.يَغْتَسِلَ: Performs the ritual bath (ghus the major ritual bath (ghusl)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting if one has sexual intercourse and sleeps before bathing until after dawn?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between the validity (sahhah) and completeness (kamal) of the fast, establishing that sexual intercourse invalidates the fast requiring qada, whereas the state of janabah (major impurity) itself does not break it. The Imam provides practical guidance on the timing of ghusl, noting that delaying the bath until after dawn does not nullify the fast, a key point in Shia fiqh regarding the conditions for fasting during Ramadan. This ruling underscores the principle that the fast is tied to the abstention from food, drink, and sexual intercourse, rather than the ritual purity state at the moment of dawn.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who touches the slave girl during the Month of Ramazan, then he sleeps before he washes. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should complete his Fast and he should make up for the Fast of that day, except if he wakes up before the emergence of the dawn. So if he waits for the water to warm up, or to be drawn, so the dawn emerges, then there is no making up for (the Fast of) his day’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked one of the two Imam, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about a man who approaches the slave-girl in the month of Ramadan; then goes to sleep without Ghusl (bath). He (the Imam) said, ‘He is required to complete that fast and fast its Qada’ (compensatory fast), unless he wakes up before dawn and waits to warm up the water or looks for water but it becomes dawn then there is no Qada’ (compensatory fast) upon him.’”
